baseline.commit_a32_subject: A32 BETA HARDWARE FINALIZER: touchscreen alive (normal-boot fix), launcher parity + cache invalidation, DECON colour conversion, ten-zone cutout safe areas, phone buttons (power/volume/Bixby), full boot animation
baseline.phone_deployment_note: The A32 hashes were recorded as verified on the target in the A32 record. This run has no live phone console (see docs/beta-finalization/preflight/ENVIRONMENT.md section 6), so the guard compares the *built* artefacts in build/out/s10plus/a32/ against those recorded hashes instead of re-reading the phone.

invariants.title: Launcher/PWA cache invalidation (A32 briq A31)
invariants.why: After an A32 deployment the previous launcher stayed alive because the service worker kept serving ./js/*.js from its old cache namespace. The invariant: a redeployed launcher is never served from a stale cache. Three legs must all hold - (a) the SW namespace is versioned and 'activate' deletes the old namespaces, (b) code assets are network-first, (c) the host purges the WebKit caches and version-stamps the launcher URL.

invariants.title: XRGB8888 -> DECON ABGR8888 colour conversion
invariants.why: The panel's DECON maps R@0 G@8 B@16 while the compositor hands the bridge XRGB8888 (R@16 G@8 B@0). Copying the words unchanged swapped red and blue on the glass. The invariant: the R<->B swap stays in the scanout path and the binary still reproduces the A32 selftest vectors.

invariants.title: Hardware button manager is the single owner of power/volume/assistant
invariants.why: A32 made one process the only handler of the gpio_keys key set (114 VOLUMEDOWN, 115 VOLUMEUP, 116 POWER, 703 assistant), so POWER short toggles the display through nuxel-wl-fb without a second framebuffer owner and volume drives the real ALSA element. The invariant: that ownership model and its service definition survive.

invariants.title: Live USB console stays reachable and respawning
invariants.why: The CDC-ACM console is the only channel that can inspect a running Nuxel without flashing and without adb. The ACM tty raises SIGHUP when a host attaches, so the supervisor must respawn the shell, and the initramfs must launch it before switch_root. The invariant: the console binary, its launch point and the host-side driver script all stay in place.

invariants.title: The full A32 offline suite still runs (soft signal while other groups edit shared suites)
invariants.why: A32's evidence is `tools/s10plus/a32/tests/run-tests.sh` exiting 0 with 0 failing suites. The guard re-runs it on every invocation so a regression in the colour selftest, the keycode bitmap decode, the safe-zone engine, the launcher registry or the wallpaper asset is visible immediately. It is a soft assertion because two of the suites it drives (safe-zones-test.js, and by extension the safe-zone engine) belong to bg-02 and are legitimately mid-flight during the parallel build: a failure there is reported as WARN naming the owning group, never as a silent pass and never as a false baseline regression.

invariants.title: Live-console host tooling and the work-queue renderer stay usable and honest
invariants.why: Two host-side tools decide whether the rest of the run can be trusted. (a) scripts/s10plus-debug-pack/nuxel-live.sh is the only channel to the handset: in session 2 it was found broken three ways on a Linux host - a missing heredoc terminator (bash warned on every invocation), macOS-only /dev/cu.usbmodem* device discovery (the Linux gadget is /dev/ttyACM*), and a port lock that crashed with a raw PermissionError traceback under sudo because Fedora's fs.protected_regular=2 forbids root from O_CREAT-opening another user's file in the sticky /tmp. (b) docs/beta-finalization/WORK-QUEUE.md is the human view of the queue; if it can drift from the JSON store, the resumed mission plans against a fiction. Both are now gated here.

invariants.title: Every asset the briQ enumerated as protected is actually pinned (nuxelctl, the libinput shim sources, the canonical assets, the Settings/Terminal PWA integration)
invariants.why: briq-00d's deliverable names the A32 assets that must not regress: nuxel-wl-fb, nuxel-pwa-host, nuxel-button-manager, nuxelctl, libnuxel-libinput-path.so, the ten-zone safe-area configuration, the Nuxel Home/Settings/Terminal PWA integration files, assets/nuxel-background.png and assets/nuxel-boot-animation.mp4. The first register revision pinned the .c/.service, the safe-zone config/engine and part of the Home PWA, but left four enumerated items with NO pin and NO assertion anywhere in the tree: (a) tools/s10plus/a32/nuxelctl - present only as metadata plus the abbreviated deployed hash 'e4281cab…' in the A32 release record, with no guard assertion; (b) the libinput-path shim sources tools/s10plus/a31/nuxel-libinput-path.c and tools/s10plus/a33/nuxel-libinput-path.c - zero occurrences in the register or the guard, even though bg-01b owns and edits the a33 copy in this same run, which is exactly the drift this register exists to catch; (c) assets/nuxel-boot-animation.mp4 - no expected-hash constant existed anywhere in the tree (tools/dedupe-assets.sh only compares copies against the canonical file and is not part of the gate); (d) the Settings/Terminal PWA integration files under pwa/nuxel-apps/settings/ and pwa/nuxel-apps/terminal/ - the launcher-registry test only checks that index.html + js exist, never their bytes. The omission was silent, which this briQ forbids, so INV-11 registers all four explicitly: drift is now a named WARN (shared files) or FAIL (baseline-owned files) instead of an invisible change. Deliberately NOT pinned, and stated so this is not a silent gap: the 0-byte '.keep' placeholder files in the two app directories (pinning an empty file proves nothing and would be noise).
